question: For each defender and season, did shooters score fewer or more field-goal points in their matchups against this defender than their own season shooting against everyone else predicts? Is that signal: do more defenders' intervals exclude zero than chance would, does it persist from season to season, and does it agree with the lineup-adjusted defensive values of courtlens-shot-decomposition-v1?
inputs: Matchups: the retained regular-season shufinskiy matchups_<year> archives 2017 to 2025 (nine seasons; none exist earlier) at the IM01/R01 pins, checked by SHA-256. Fields: game_id, team_id, home_team_id, away_team_id, person_id, matchups_person_id, matchup_field_goals_attempted, matchup_field_goals_made, matchup_three_pointers_attempted, matchup_three_pointers_made. Tables were built before this registration by courtlens.evaluation.defensive_shot_quality_data (two builds, identical hashes) and pinned in parameters.table_sha256.
Priors: R03's frozen league Beta priors for 2P% and 3P% for the target season (courtlens-signal-noise-v1, fitted on the three earlier seasons only).

Part A: courtlens-shot-decomposition-v1's frozen results (results SHA-256 in parameters), for the reported agreement check only. Part A's defensive values are lineup-adjusted and were read as league summaries and persistence before this registration; no matchup value had been computed.

DATA CHECK (done before this registration; counts only, no defender value). Orientation: person_id is the shooter and matchups_person_id the defender: player totals of person_id against the shot chart correlate 0.999 (FGA 2017-18), 0.997 (FGA 2025-26), 0.999 and 0.998 (3PA); matchups_person_id only 0.86 and 0.72 to 0.75. Games per season 2017-18 to 2025-26: 1,222, 1,223, 967, 1,080, 1,229, 1,230, 1,227, 1,229, 1,230 (2019-20 has 1,059 scheduled games, so it lacks 92). Rows: 181,840 to 240,839 per season, about half with no attempt (kept out of the table, counted). Every row's points equal its field-goal points plus free throws made. Double credit: matchup FGA total 8% to 12% more than the shot chart in the same games. The excess is in 2-pointers (2PA and 2PM both about 13% to 20% over the chart, at an ordinary make rate, e.g. 2022-23 160,374 / 86,871 against 132,952 / 72,841), while 3PA and 3PM are within about 3%, so some 2-pointers appear credited to more than one defender; they do not look like fouled misses. Help-defender columns are zero in every row of every season, so no second-defender value can be built.
method: RULE. For a shooter o and defender d in a season, the expected make rate for 2s and for 3s separately is the Beta posterior mean (alpha_t + M) / (alpha_t + beta_t + A), with alpha_t, beta_t R03's prior for that stat and season and M, A o's matchup makes and attempts in that season against EVERY DEFENDER EXCEPT d. Excluding only the attempts on d, not whole games: it removes the defender's own influence on the prediction and keeps the shooter's other attempts in those games. Expected points of d's matchups = sum over rows of 2 * FGA2 * p2 + 3 * FGA3 * p3. Actual = 2 * FGM2 + 3 * FGM3. Field-goal points only, as Part A and R05: free throws are excluded because a foul drawn is not in these counts by shot type.
HINDSIGHT. This is descriptive and uses the whole season, including games after the matchup. It predicts nothing and feeds no forecast.

D-SQ. L_t = (sum expected - sum actual) / sum FGA over all rows of the season, the league term that removes the leave-out and shrinkage offset. D-SQ of d = 100 * ((expected - actual) / FGA - L_t), points per 100 matchup attempts. POSITIVE IS GOOD: shooters scored less than their own shooting predicts. Computed for all attempts, 2-pointers and 3-pointers, each with its own term.

MINIMUM VOLUME. D-SQ needs at least 300 matchup FGA in the season; otherwise status small_sample and no value. The 2PT and 3PT views also need at least 100 attempts of that type, otherwise unknown. Measured defender counts at 300+: 281 to 329 per season.

KEY MATCHUPS. For each served defender, the five shooters with the most attempts against him (ties by id): attempts, actual PPS and the expected PPS above. Descriptive; no interval. Small samples, never a verdict.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE, STATED ON THE PAGE. Databallr's card uses ShotQuality's tracking: closest defender and 2nd defender attempts, and opponent shot-quality expected value. Free data has no closest-defender feed, the help columns are empty, and matchup rows have no shot location, so CourtLens's 'expected PPS' is what the shooters' own shooting predicts, NOT a look-quality estimate; R05's model cannot be applied to matchups. The card's RAPM headline is dSQ from courtlens-shot-decomposition-v1 for 2022-23 onward and unknown before.
SIGNAL CHECK (reported, no gate). The number of served defender-seasons whose 95% interval excludes zero, against the 5% expected if no defender differed.

PERSISTENCE (reported, no gate). Consecutive served seasons, eight pairs from 2017-18 to 2025-26 pooled, players served in both, Pearson correlation weighted by the harmonic mean of matchup FGA, for D-SQ, expected PPS and actual PPS.

AGREEMENT (reported, no gate). Same player and season, 2022-23 to 2025-26, both served: weighted correlation (harmonic mean of matchup FGA and Part A defence shots) of D-SQ with dSQ, dContest and dTS.
RUN ORDER. No choice is made, so one pass. Any change after results are read is disclosed; analysis changes require v2. Timings are in the run log only.
CREDIT. The card layout and the concept are Databallr's D-ShotQuality page; ShotQuality owns the tracking-based values, not used here. Matchup data: NBA Stats via shufinskiy/nba_data.
selection: None. The rule, minimums and every reported check are fixed here, before any defender value is computed.
uncertainty: D-SQ intervals: 2,000-replicate bootstrap of the defender's own games (seed SeedSequence([7007, starting year, kind index, player id])), 95% percentile, with each shooter's expected rate and the league term held fixed: they show matchup-outcome noise, not uncertainty in the expectation. Correlations: player-cluster bootstrap, 2,000 replicates, seed 7007 for persistence and 7008 for agreement, 95% percentile. Overlapping intervals do not rank two defenders.
evaluation: Per season: games, league FGA, PPS, expected PPS and term by kind; defenders and those served; intervals excluding zero; median interval width.
Pooled signal share, persistence and agreement with intervals.
Reproducibility: two runs give the same results hash.
acceptance: Descriptive: there is no gate. The run fails on a changed table, a changed Part A file, an unusable prior, a non-finite value or a constant that differs from this registration.
Every defender-season has a status, and every value an interval or a named unknown.
Two runs give the same results hash.
Published whichever way it goes, including no signal or no persistence.
outputs: docs/evidence/research/r06/ (receipt, data check, per-season summaries, signal, persistence, agreement)
limitations: Matchup assignment is the NBA's tracking-based estimate of who guarded whom. A defender is assigned tough or easy shooters by his team's scheme; using each shooter's own rate addresses that, but not the difficulty of the specific shots, teammates' help or the team's rim protection.
Some 2-pointers are credited to more than one defender, so 'shots defended' overstates distinct shots.
No shot location or contest data: this measures opponents' results against their norm, not the quality of the looks allowed.
3-point results are very noisy: R03 found 3P% does not stabilize at normal volumes. Intervals show game sampling only.
2019-20 lacks the games after the hiatus; 2017-18 to 2024-25 lack up to eight games each.
The expected rate is shrunk toward a league prior, not a positional one.
negative_result_policy: Publish every number whatever it shows, including no signal, no persistence or disagreement with Part A.
